chunks: An evil act is like a rotten tree torn out of the earth with no (base or) firmness.
ai.seo_question: What is the metaphorical meaning of the evil word compared to a tree in the Quran?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse (14:25) is often interpreted as describing the false claims of polytheists or the transient nature of evil ideologies that lack divine grounding. The metaphor of a tree 'uprooted from above' signifies a complete and irreversible destruction, contrasting with the firm root of the 'good word' mentioned in the subsequent verse. This highlights the ultimate instability of worldly falsehoods compared to the enduring truth of monotheism.
